question.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/f1124e83e3b7614557a1a6de54523cc99f62ba2a52af1da8e4d22e14466ce020.svg)
If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_2?$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/a185a6fd91c78ed3e291b3ac8b99f9430290e5d8c1060a7d97317efc230aeb40.svg)

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/1e780d384ca1fd957d742bbd047399c558ab016d187ce4cf71682546673aba35.svg)
This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=6$ and $y_2=4.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/58da62903247cf6dfdf33be86293c181ef5184048ca7cd6c921360e5d202f353.svg)

- Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/e0563dde4944ecbe2ccb98bc91246fa18c7a808df96ab77f9f8efb5510084677.svg)
This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $x_2=-2$ and $x_1=2.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/a84088cff2a3589652ef7cabf09e3d8429fad7797ea20d44a416f85dcc7f9b65.svg)

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_2 = 2 \cdot 4 = 8.$
